items.q:
Identify the missing word in the following sentence.
A [?] is a means of enabling value co-creation by facilitating outcomes that customers want to achieve, without the customer having to manage specific costs and risks.
items.x: This is the definition of a service. A product is a configuration of resources, and a service offering is a formal description of services for a target consumer group.

items.q:
Which two statements about service consumer roles are CORRECT?
1. The customer defines the requirements and takes responsibility for the outcomes of service consumption
2. The user authorizes the budget for service consumption
3. The sponsor authorizes the budget for service consumption
4. The sponsor must always be a user of the service
items.x: The customer defines requirements and owns outcomes, and the sponsor authorizes the budget. Users use the service. A sponsor may or may not also be a user.

items.q: Which of the following is an example of value for SOCIETY and the community?
o: Employment and taxes paid by the organization
items.x: Value differs by stakeholder. Society and the community benefit from employment, taxes and the organization's contribution to the community.

items.q: An employee is loaned a company laptop that remains company property. Within the IT department's service offering, what is the use of the laptop?
items.x: Because ownership is not transferred, using the loaned laptop is access to resources. If the laptop became the employee's property, it would be goods.

items.q: Organization B uses a cloud service from Organization A to create its own online service, which it offers to Organization C. What does this illustrate?
o: The service relationship model, in which organizations are both consumers and providers in a chain
A value stream that only involves one organization
items.x: In the service relationship model, the resources a consumer gains from one service become part of the products and services it offers to others, creating chains or networks of service relationships.

items.q: An airline offers a mobile check-in app. Which of the following is an OUTCOME for a passenger?
o: The passenger reaches the gate on time without queueing
A boarding pass file is generated
The app sends a push notification
The app stores the passenger's preferences
items.x: An outcome is a result for a stakeholder enabled by outputs. Boarding passes, notifications and stored preferences are outputs. Getting to the gate on time without queueing is what the passenger wants to achieve.

items.q: A service can be resumed at an alternative site within four hours after a disaster. Which quality does this describe?
items.x: Continuity is a warranty aspect, along with availability, capacity and security. Warranty is assurance that a product or service will meet agreed requirements.

items.q: A service is extremely reliable and always available, but it does not provide the features users need. What is the MOST likely result?
o: The service creates high value because warranty is more important
The service creates value as long as it is cheap
The service creates little value, because both utility and warranty are needed
items.x: Value requires both fitness for purpose (utility) and fitness for use (warranty). High warranty cannot make up for missing functionality.

items.q: Every Monday morning, ten users report the same application error, which is fixed each time by a restart. How should the underlying cause of these reports be recorded?
items.x: Each report is an incident. The recurring underlying cause is a problem, meaning a cause or potential cause of one or more incidents, and problem management should investigate it.

items.q: While a problem is being investigated, the service desk restarts the affected service to restore it for users each time. What is the restart?
items.x: A workaround reduces or eliminates the impact of an incident or problem for which a full resolution is not yet available. It is usually recorded in the known error record.

items.q: A user asks the service desk how to share a calendar with a colleague. How should this be classified?
o: As a service request for information
items.x: Requests for information are a type of service request: a normal, pre-defined part of service delivery. Nothing is broken, so it is not an incident.

items.q: Which statement about sustainability in ITIL (Version 5) is CORRECT?
o: It is considered only when a product is retired
It should be considered throughout the lifecycle, for example in design decisions, acquisition choices and operations
It concerns only the cost of a product
It is the responsibility of suppliers alone
items.x: Sustainability, covering environmental, social and economic impact, is part of overall quality and should influence decisions throughout the lifecycle, alongside utility, warranty and experience.

items.q: Which is the ITIL definition of a process?
o: A set of interrelated or interacting activities that transform inputs into outputs
A series of steps to create and deliver products and services to consumers
A set of organizational resources for performing work
items.x: A process transforms inputs into outputs and defines the sequence of actions and their dependencies. It belongs to the value streams and processes dimension. Option B is a value stream and option C is a practice.

items.q: Staff increasingly need broad knowledge across several areas combined with deep expertise in one specialism. Which dimension does this consideration MAINLY belong to?
items.x: Competencies and skills, including broad knowledge combined with deep specialism (often called a 'T-shaped' profile), are part of the organizations and people dimension.

items.q: A company concludes that buying a managed service is cheaper than building and running the capability itself. Which factor influencing supplier strategy is this?
items.x: Cost concerns, meaning whether it is more economical to buy than to build and operate, are one of the factors influencing supplier strategy.

items.q: Rapid advances in generative AI are changing how organizations provide user support. Under PESTLE, which type of external factor is this?
items.x: Advances in technologies such as AI, cloud and automation are Technological factors that influence all four dimensions.

items.q: An organization opens its live product to a new group of customers, makes sure they can access and use it as agreed, and onboards them. Which lifecycle activity is this?
items.x: Deliver makes products and services available and usable for consumers as agreed, including onboarding. Operate keeps the product running, and Support handles issues and restoration.

items.q: Patterns found in support data and user feedback suggest a valuable new feature. In which lifecycle activity would this opportunity MAINLY be explored?
items.x: Discover explores needs, demand signals and opportunities, wherever they come from, including insights from Operate and Support, and aligns them with strategy before resources are committed.

items.q: A team writes code, runs automated tests and produces a tested software package ready for deployment. Which lifecycle activity is this?
items.x: Build creates, configures and tests solutions. Moving the tested package into the live environment would then be Transition.

items.q: An organization never develops software and buys all of its products as SaaS. Which statement about the product and service lifecycle is CORRECT?
o: The lifecycle does not apply to the organization
The lifecycle still applies: the organization still discovers needs, acquires, configures, transitions, operates, delivers and supports products
items.x: The lifecycle applies whether products are built or bought. An organization that builds nothing still performs activities such as Acquire, Transition, Operate, Deliver and Support.

items.q: A team is asked to produce a new management report. According to 'focus on value', what should the team establish FIRST?
o: Which tool will produce the report
How many pages the report should have
How fast the report can be automated
Who will consume the report and what value they need from it
items.x: Applying 'focus on value' starts with knowing who the consumer is and understanding what they value, so that the output enables useful outcomes.

items.q: A new manager wants to discard all existing processes immediately, without assessing them, and design everything from scratch. Which guiding principle is being ignored?
items.x: 'Start where you are' advises against starting from scratch without considering what is already available. The current state should be assessed objectively first.

items.q: According to 'progress iteratively with feedback', when should feedback be sought?
o: Before, throughout and after each iteration
Only at the end of the whole initiative
items.x: Seeking and using feedback at every stage keeps the work focused and appropriate, even when circumstances change.

items.q: Which statement about collaboration is CORRECT according to the guiding principles?
o: Collaboration should be limited to the IT department
Only managers should be involved in decisions
The right stakeholders should be involved at the right level, including customers, users, suppliers and other teams
Collaboration requires that everyone agrees before any action is taken
items.x: 'Collaborate and promote visibility' involves the right people in the right roles, including external parties, and it does not require consensus.

items.q: A security team introduces a strict password policy without considering its effect on the service desk workload and on users' daily work. Which guiding principle was MOST clearly neglected?
items.x: Changing one element without considering its effect on the rest of the system, such as people, processes and support, causes problems. 'Think and work holistically' asks teams to consider the whole.

items.q: Managers want detailed data on every request, but staff say that filling in long forms wastes their time. Which guiding principle MOST directly helps to resolve this conflict?
items.x: 'Keep it simple and practical' recognizes that objectives can conflict, and recommends agreeing what is truly needed and finding the simplest workable balance.

items.q: In ITIL, what is automation?
o: The use of technology to perform a step or series of steps correctly and consistently with limited or no human intervention
The replacement of all staff with AI
items.x: Automation uses technology to perform steps correctly and consistently with limited or no human intervention. It should follow simplification and optimization.

items.q: Which statement about the governing body is CORRECT?
o: It manages the daily work of support teams
It is responsible for writing code
It is accountable for the organization's compliance with policies and external regulations
It only exists in public-sector organizations
items.x: The governing body is accountable at the highest level for the organization's performance and compliance, including with external regulations.

items.q: The board reviews changes in the market and in stakeholder needs to assess whether the current strategy is still appropriate. Which governance activity is this?
items.x: 'Evaluate' assesses the organization, its strategy, portfolios and relationships as circumstances change. Directing and monitoring follow from it.

items.q: Which of the following is an example of continual improvement at TEAM level?
o: Only the board approving a new strategy
Waiting for an annual audit before changing anything
Hiring consultants to fix all problems
A team logging ideas in its improvement register and implementing small improvements in each work cycle
items.x: Continual improvement happens at all levels. Teams can manage their own improvement backlog and deliver small improvements regularly, while larger initiatives are coordinated across the organization.

items.q: Which information is typically recorded for each improvement idea in a continual improvement register?
o: A description of the idea, its expected value or benefit, its priority, its status and an owner
Only the name of the person who suggested it
The incident number and the user's phone number
The configuration of the affected servers
items.x: A CIR tracks improvement ideas so that they can be assessed, prioritized and progressed. Typical information includes the description, expected value, priority, status and owner.

items.q: After a successful improvement, staff gradually return to their old ways of working. Which step of the continual improvement model is meant to prevent this?
o: How do we keep the momentum going?
items.x: 'How do we keep the momentum going?' embeds the change through communication, reinforcement and recognition, so that improvements last and new ones follow.

items.q: What is the purpose of the relationship management practice?
o: To establish and nurture the links between the organization and its stakeholders at strategic and tactical levels
items.x: Relationship management builds and maintains relationships with stakeholders. It identifies their needs, handles escalations and makes sure products and services facilitate value.

items.q: What is the purpose of the information security management practice?
o: To ensure that services are available when needed
To make sure that suppliers are paid on time
To protect the information needed by the organization to conduct its business
items.x: Information security management protects the information the organization needs. This includes confidentiality, integrity and availability, and a balance of prevention, detection and correction.

items.q: Which component of the ITIL value system provides recommendations that guide an organization in all circumstances, regardless of changes in its goals, strategies, type of work or management structure?
items.x: This is the definition of a guiding principle. The seven guiding principles are universal and enduring.

items.q: Which component of the ITIL value system is the means by which an organization is directed and controlled?
items.x: Governance is how the organization is directed and controlled, through evaluate, direct and monitor. It sets the direction within which the other components operate.

items.q: In value stream mapping, what does the metric '% complete and accurate' indicate?
o: The percentage of staff who completed training
The percentage of time a step is busy
The percentage of the budget that has been spent
How often the output of a step can be used by the next step without rework or corrections
items.x: % complete and accurate measures the quality of hand-offs between steps. Low values reveal rework and its hidden cost to the flow.

items.q: A customer orders a product online and receives it at home. How would this value stream BEST be classified?
items.x: Core value streams deliver products and services directly to external consumers. Enabling value streams, such as hiring or onboarding staff, support the core value streams internally.

items.q: An AI tool drafts new knowledge articles from the notes of resolved incidents. Which capability of the ITIL AI Capability Model is MAINLY demonstrated?
items.x: Creation is about generating new content, such as text, code, images or drafts. Curation would be organizing and maintaining existing knowledge, for example reviewing and retiring outdated articles.

items.q: Which statement BEST describes site reliability engineering (SRE) in relation to ITIL?
o: SRE applies software engineering to operations, using service level objectives and error budgets to balance reliability with the speed of change, and it can complement ITIL practices
SRE is a replacement for all ITIL management practices
SRE is a certification for organizations
SRE is only used for hardware maintenance
items.x: SRE, which originated at Google, uses engineering practices, SLOs and error budgets to run reliable services. It fits well alongside ITIL activities such as Operate and Support and practices such as service level management.
